title: Inspect the PO Register
scenario: It is 10:10 AM. The invoice claims 500 bolts at $2.44 each. Says who? The Purchase Order Register is Beacon's own record of what was actually ordered and agreed. Inspect PO-7742 - the order this invoice claims to bill against - and learn how the desk uses it as the anchor for matching.
input: PO-7742 | Vendor: V-1042 Northwind Fasteners | Line: M8 hex bolt, zinc | Quantity ordered: 500 | Unit price (PO): 2.40 | PO total: 1200.00 | Owned by: Procurement Lead. The PO number is the join key - it links the invoice to this order and to the goods receipt.
instructions: Read the PO Register as Beacon's own record of what was agreed, not the vendor's claim.
Tag each field to the value that holds it in the register - watch the PO price versus the invoice claim.
Validate to mint the PO source profile.

fields.label: Join key (PO number)
fields.explain: The join key is the identifier the whole three-way match is anchored on - the number the invoice cites and the receipt posts against.

fields.label: Vendor
fields.explain: Tag the vendor Beacon ordered from, not the item description - the register names who the order was placed with.

fields.label: Quantity ordered
fields.explain: Tag the count the PO agreed to - the ordered quantity the invoice and receipt are checked against.

fields.label: Agreed unit price
fields.explain: The agreed price is the PO's own figure, not the 2.44 the invoice claims. The gap between them is exactly what the tolerance check judges.

fields.label: PO total
fields.explain: Tag the order value Beacon committed to - the PO total the agreed line quantities roll up to.

copilotPrompt: Explain how a purchase-order register anchors invoice matching: what the PO number joins, why the PO price is the agreement rather than the invoice claim, who owns it, and which step consumes it first.
successMessage: PO inspected. You now hold the agreed order the invoice will be matched against.

intro.heading: Before you match: anchor on the order

sections.title: The PO is the agreement
sections.body: A purchase order records what Beacon and the vendor agreed to buy and at what price. When an invoice arrives, it is a claim - the PO is the trusted baseline it must reconcile against.

sections.title: One number joins three documents
sections.body: PO-7742 appears on the invoice, on the goods receipt, and in the register. That shared key is what lets the workflow line up all three legs of the match automatically.

sections.title: Price disagreements are expected
sections.body: The PO says 2.40; the invoice says 2.44. That gap is not an error to hide - it is the exact question the tolerance policy will answer two steps from now.

sections.title: What you produce here
sections.body: Passing the inspection mints a PO source profile: the ordered quantity, agreed price, owner, and join key the match will rely on.

realWorld.soloRebuildPath: You'd pull the matching purchase order from the PO log so you can check the invoice against what was actually ordered.

tools.powerAutomate: 'Get items' filtered by PO number from the PO list
tools.python: look up the PO by number in the register table

takeaway.heading: PO inspected
points: You tagged each field in the PO register: join key, vendor, quantity, agreed price, and total.
The PO number is the anchor that joins invoice, PO, and receipt into one matchable set.
The PO price is the agreement; the invoice price is a claim the tolerance check will judge.
Your PO source profile is stored - the ordered quantity and agreed price the match depends on.
The workflow can now anchor every invoice against what was actually ordered.
